forecasts.reason: +6 steps costs about 0.13 s and should buy about 0.05–0.12 pp. That is at the edge of a 20-seed SE of 0.07 pp, so the 0.7545 gate is a coin flip.
Freezing group 2 saves about 0.24 s and the top-up costs about 0.13 s, so time should drop about 2%, right at the threshold. Parity within 0.03 pp can't be resolved at a 20-seed SE of 0.07 pp.
Of the 135 ms of non-step work, maybe 40–80 ms is removable. The math is identical, so this should be a small time win with accuracy at rebuild noise.
It adds about 1 ms per step on 231 unfrozen steps (+0.2 s). The gain is likely ≤0.1 pp, about the dial's rate, so it won't clearly beat the dial.
The fused kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU likely saves under 3%. ReLU usually costs CIFAR-100 accuracy (about 0.2 pp).

cruxes: What is the post-freeze epoch dial's true rate, measured on the same build over 20 seeds (I074)? If +0.25 epoch buys at least 0.12 pp for 0.13 s, then the group-2 freeze plus a top-up dominates the tip. If it buys under 0.06 pp, no margin can be bought.
How much did E046 lose on held-out seeds against a same-build baseline? A loss of 0.1 pp or less makes I075 a clear win; 0.2 pp or more closes the cascade.
Is the 68 ms of copies (I076) avoidable cudagraph copy-in, or work inherent to the data path? That decides whether a free saving of about 1–1.5% exists.
structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E047. The tip is E036: 231 steps, 5.31 s, and a population mean of about 0.7525–0.7535, so a null change has roughly a 35–40% chance of clearing the gate.

Time model: time ≈ 0.25 s + Σ(step costs). Per step: 32 px 0.032 s, frozen-stem 32 px about 0.0235 s, frozen group 2 about 0.0135 s, 20 px 0.016 s. Non-step GPU work is about 0.135 s, partly removable.

No time-neutral booster has worked (6 of 6 were ≤0). The cheapest remaining lever is backward truncation, provided it is bought back with epochs. The dial's rate is about 1–2.5 s/pp. Systems-only cuts of 1–2% are the only free money left.
